findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c and ab77 an AC requiring each shard to measure (by diff line-count) and record its actual recovered comment lines on its own ticket
evidence: Parent (superseded): 'Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards.'
9ce8's corrected AC: 'The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the unreliable ~970 estimate.'

The four ACs of 4b94/4fc1/ad16/da4c/ab77 are only: non-KEEP relocated/deleted; do_not_move appended; stale corrected/deleted; no load-bearing invariant lost - none require measuring or recording recovered line counts.
Absence test: no sibling AC in the roster delivers per-shard line measurement for these five shards.
findings.finding: Parent AC 'Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered' is uncovered for five of six children - only 9ce8 carries a measure-and-record AC.
scenarios: A shard lands its edits without recording its recovered line count on its ticket; the parent cannot compute the net total across shards and the completion verifier for parent AC#2 has no per-shard datum to sum.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to each of the five children's ACs the 9ce8-style line: 'The ACTUAL recovered comment-line count is measured (by diff line-count) and recorded on this ticket.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16 and ab77 an AC requiring each shard's enumerated new ADRs (and amendments) to exist and be committed before any comment citing them is collapsed
evidence: Parent (superseded): 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets ... EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that shard's own enumerated ADR set.'
9ce8's corrected AC: 'Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed or deleted -- destination first, then the relocation'.
4b94 body: 'capabilities.py:166-198 is structurally a complete ADR ... NO ADR in the 83-file corpus mentions web search' - a new ADR destination.
4fc1 body: 'New ADR proposed: Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation'.
ad16 body: 'Three new ADRs: the unversioned additive-only attestation manifest; the Burr tripwire; gate context is never elided'.
ab77 body: 'Three new ADRs proposed from review_bot/: bounded shutdown; the deploy-safe in-flight counter; retryable coverage gaps'.
The four ACs of these children contain no destination-first / ADR-exists-before-collapse requirement; absence test finds no sibling delivering it for these shards.
findings.finding: Parent AC 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed' is uncovered for five of six children - only 9ce8 carries a destination-first ADR-ordering AC, yet 4b94, 4fc1, ad16 and ab77 each propose new ADRs to be cited.
scenarios: A comment citing 'see ADR NNNN' is collapsed in the 4b94/4fc1/ad16/ab77 shard before ADR NNNN is written and committed; the citation dangles and the relocated argument is lost, exactly the failure 9ce8's correction guards against.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 9ce8 AC verbatim to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16 and ab77: 'Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed or deleted -- destination first, then the relocation.'

findings.finding: Parent AC2 (each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered) is covered by only one of six children. Only 9ce8's corrected AC ('The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket') delivers the measure-and-record outcome. The other five children (4b94, 4fc1, ab77, ad16, da4c) have no acceptance criterion requiring measurement or recording of recovered lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Replicate 9ce8's 'measured and recorded on this ticket' AC into the other five children so the parent can aggregate the net total.

findings.finding: Parent AC3 (every enumerated ADR and amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any citing comment is collapsed — destination-first) is covered by only one of six children. Four children propose NEW ADRs to serve as citation destinations — 4b94 (web-search capabilities ADR), 4fc1 ('Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation'), ab77 (three review_bot ADRs), ad16 (three ADRs incl. attestation manifest, Burr tripwire, gate-context) — yet none of those four carry an AC gating comment collapse on the ADR existing first. Only 9ce8's corrected AC states the destination-first ordering for its ADRs/amendments.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy 9ce8's destination-first ADR AC into 4b94, 4fc1, ab77, and ad16 against each shard's own enumerated ADR set.

findings.finding: The parent AC requiring each shard to MEASURE and RECORD the actual recovered comment-line count on its own ticket is delivered by only one sibling (9ce8). The other five shards' acceptance criteria do not include a measure-and-record obligation.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c, and ab77 the same measure-and-record AC 9ce8 carries, framed as an output not a target.

findings.finding: The parent AC requiring every enumerated new ADR / amendment to EXIST AND BE COMMITTED before any citing comment is collapsed ('destination first, then relocation') is delivered by only one sibling (9ce8). The other five shards each propose new ADRs but carry no ADR-ordering AC.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy 9ce8's 'destination first, then relocation' ADR-ordering AC into the other five shard tickets, scoped to each shard's own enumerated ADR set.

findings.finding: Destination-first / consumer-impact gap for DOC homes (analogous to the ADR gap but not covered by parent AC3, which enumerates only ADRs). 4fc1 relocates ~126 lines of stale bash-migration prose to docs/bash-migration.md; ab77 states docs/config.md rows must be WRITTEN FIRST before trimming _config_schema.py or 'the trim destroys documentation'; da4c notes docs/event-schema.md is a PARTIAL, STALE copy ('two homes, one drifting'). None of these three children carry an AC gating the comment collapse/relocation on the destination doc existing and being complete first.
findings.suggested_fix: Generalise parent AC3 (and the relevant children) from 'ADR' to 'ADR or documentation destination' so doc relocations are gated destination-first too.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC to each child (at minimum ad16, which names untracked follow-ups) requiring that history citing no ticket has a ticket filed before its block is reduced to a citation
evidence: Parent (superseded): 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first.'
ad16 body: 'Only two are costly: untracked follow-ups in production_batch_runner.py that must be filed first.' - but ad16's ACs do not include a file-first requirement.
None of the six children's four generic ACs mention history-without-a-ticket or ticket-filing-first; absence test finds no sibling covering it.
findings.finding: Parent AC 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first' is uncovered by every child - no sibling's ACs mention filing a ticket for untracked history before collapse, though ad16 flags untracked follow-ups that 'must be filed first'.
scenarios: A history comment citing no ticket is reduced to a bare citation in any shard without first filing the ticket the citation should point to, producing a dangling citation and lost history - contradicting the parent's file-first requirement.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to each child: 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first (destination before collapse).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to every child an AC that the full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged, and that inline pragmas and test-introspected docstrings are placed on the shard's do_not_move list
evidence: Parent (superseded): 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (# noqa, # type: ignore, # ruff:, # tickets-boundary-ok) and any docstring a test reads via introspection are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's do_not_move list.'
9ce8 corrected AC: 'No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged' - narrows to tests only, omits make lint / make typecheck and the pragma/introspected-docstring rule.
The other five children have no test/lint/typecheck AC at all; their four generic ACs never mention pragmas or introspected docstrings.

Absence test: no sibling AC delivers the lint+typecheck-pass or pragma-preservation outcome; ab77 and da4c bodies do note specific pragma/introspection risks (# read-via: markers in ab77, noqa suffix in da4c) but with no covering AC.
findings.finding: Parent AC 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged across every shard' with pragmas and introspected docstrings on every shard's do_not_move list is uncovered for five children and scope-narrowed for 9ce8.
scenarios: A shard relocates a # noqa or # type: ignore pragma as if it were narrative prose, breaking make lint or make typecheck, and no shard AC catches it (the parent 'across every shard' requirement is not inherited).
ab77's # read-via: markers (a CI gate) or a test-introspected docstring are deleted; CI breaks but no child AC required test+lint+typecheck to pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parent's full behaviour-change AC (test suite + make lint + make typecheck pass; pragmas and introspected docstrings on do_not_move) to all six children, replacing 9ce8's narrowed 'reconciler's tests pass unchanged'.

findings.finding: Parent AC4 (history that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first) is uncovered — no child's acceptance criteria deliver it. Child bodies discuss it (ad16: '36 of 38 history blocks already cite a ticket ... two costly untracked follow-ups that must be filed first'; 4b94: '85 lines are free wins — history already citing b690...'; 9ce8: history reductions) but none of the six children's AC lists contain a history-to-citation-or-file-ticket criterion. Child AC (a) 'relocated or deleted per its destination' is a related/precursor outcome, not the same measurable outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parent's AC4 wording as an explicit criterion on each of the six children.

findings.finding: Parent AC8 (no behaviour change: full test suite AND make lint/typecheck pass unchanged across every shard; and pragma comments plus introspected docstrings go on every shard's do_not_move list) is only partially and narrowly covered. Only 9ce8 has any test AC and it is scope-narrowed to 'the reconciler's tests pass unchanged' (tests only, not lint/typecheck). No child AC mentions make lint / make typecheck, and NO child AC lists inline pragma comments (# noqa, # type: ignore, # ruff:, # tickets-boundary-ok) or test-introspected docstrings as load-bearing / do_not_move members.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy the parent's AC8 (including the pragma/introspected-docstring clause) onto all six children, broadening 9ce8's tests-only AC to include lint/typecheck.

findings.finding: The parent AC 'No behaviour change: the full test suite passes unchanged across every shard' is covered by only one sibling. 9ce8 carries 'No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged'; the other five shards carry no test-passing / no-behaviour-change AC at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 9ce8's no-behaviour-change AC (scoped to each shard's touched subtree, or the full suite) to the other five shard tickets.

findings.finding: The parent AC 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first' is covered by NO sibling's acceptance criteria. Two shards mention the behaviour in prose (4b94 'history already citing b690...'; ad16 'untracked follow-ups ... that must be filed first') but neither states it as an AC, and the other four shards are silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parent's history AC verbatim to each shard ticket that relocates history blocks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restore the '; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim' clause to the load-bearing-invariant AC in 4fc1, ab77 and da4c
evidence: Parent (superseded): 'No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim.'
4fc1, ab77, da4c ACs read only: 'No load-bearing invariant is lost' - the verbatim-preservation clause is dropped.
4b94, 9ce8, ad16 ACs keep the full '; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim' clause.

da4c body itself flags the highest-risk verbatim case: 'four SNAPSHOT-restore migration guards where relocating the rationale makes live guards look like dead defensive code' - precisely a verbatim-preservation concern its own AC no longer states.
ab77 body flags '# read-via:' machine-consumed markers as verbatim-critical, but its AC omits the verbatim clause.
findings.finding: Parent AC 'No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim' is scope-narrowed in three children whose AC drops the 'measured-fact / anti-refactor verbatim' clause.
scenarios: In da4c a measured-fact / anti-refactor guard rationale is paraphrased during relocation rather than kept verbatim; the shard still passes its narrowed 'no load-bearing invariant lost' AC because verbatim preservation was not required, yet the parent required it.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC in 4fc1, ab77 and da4c to the full parent form: 'No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Disambiguate every bare ADR number cited as an amendment/citation destination by full slug (e.g. `0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md` vs `0031-schema-derived-typeddicts.md`; the specific `0035-*` file), since ADR 0031 and 0035 each resolve to multiple distinct committed ADRs.
evidence: docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md and docs/adr/0031-schema-derived-typeddicts.md both exist (two ADR 0031s)
docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md, 0035-code-review-two-lane-tier-tagged-impact.md, and 0035-rc2b-snapshot-horizon-safe-replay.md all exist (three ADR 0035s)
The reconciler shard carries the comments the plan says cite ADR 0031/0035 (ref-lock, vendor-adapter, three-way-merge topics), so the collision is on the exact shard that consumes these references
The plan mitigates by saying the AC is 'met per-shard against that shard's own enumerated ADR set,' but the parent text itself asserts an ambiguous bare-number reference
findings.finding: The superseding AC names bare ADR numbers ('the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035') as citation/amendment destinations, but ADR 0031 and 0035 each resolve to MULTIPLE distinct committed ADRs in docs/adr, so an executor collapsing a reconciler comment to 'see ADR 0031' cannot deterministically pick the intended ADR.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (supersedes...), AC: 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035)'
scenarios: A reconciler-shard agent collapses an inline block to a one-line citation 'see ADR 0031' and links or amends the wrong ADR (schema-derived-typeddicts instead of reconciler-ref-lock)
The 'destination first, then relocation' ordering AC is checked against the wrong ADR file
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035' with fully-slugged filenames (e.g. `0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md`, `0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`) and require each shard ticket's enumerated ADR set to cite ADRs by filename, never by bare number.

findings.finding: The disposition vocabulary the acceptance criteria depend on ('non-KEEP unit') is never enumerated: the destination taxonomy (history/architecture/logic/contracts) is fully defined, but the per-unit DISPOSITION set an executor must verify completeness against -- KEEP vs relocate vs delete vs correct-in-place vs do_not_move -- and the definition of a 'unit' are left undefined, and KEEP vs do_not_move vs correct-stale overlap ambiguously.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (supersedes) AC-2 ('every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly dispositioned'); mirrored in shard 9ce8 ('Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination')
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Disposition vocabulary' subsection defining a unit (a contiguous comment block) and the exhaustive disposition labels, mapping each to its destination and to whether it is KEEP or non-KEEP, and clarify that DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-in-place are KEEP-class (retained, not counted as recovered lines) while the four RELOCATE/MOVE/DELETE classes are non-KEEP.
